answer: No seat runs uncovered: a newcomer buys cover from an established, non-kin underwriter, and each underwriter backs only a few seats before its bond is committed. Capacity is a shared, inelastic trellis: the first clone pays little, later ones bid against incumbents, so a fleet of k drains the market and pays k-squared in premiums. Policies are seat-bound and claims settle on a clear quartz ledger peers can replay, so one default burns the underwriter's book. Capacity tops out at a low zenith; past it the fleet bids against itself, while an honest newcomer buys one policy at the quoted rate.
